<p>I’m in a car speeding down the road, rereading the documents the manager sent me.</p><p>‘Hmm… renting out an entire hotel for protection?’</p><p>Out of the 20 protection personnel, there are a couple of names I recognize.</p><p>Lee Seung-jun and Min Se-rin are both on the protection team, and Min Se-rin and I are even paired together as a two-person unit.</p><p>I guess they put us on the same team because we’ve worked together before.</p><p>‘If we’re talking about large-scale combat, there really isn’t a Hunter better than Lee Seung-jun…’</p><p>At first, I thought this was a sweet gig, but then I saw that six of the protection personnel are from the Intelligence Bureau. Add Lee Seung-jun, a former Bureau member, and that’s seven.</p><p>Seeing seven A-rank human butchers—who are terrifyingly good at killing—on the list sent a chill down my spine.</p><p>‘Did the manager trick me?’</p><p>The documents didn’t have much detail about the Chungnam Branch Director, so I tried searching online, but the security was too tight—I didn’t get anything useful.</p><p>The only place I managed to dig up info was the Hunter Gallery.</p><p>I reread the post I’d screenshotted from there.</p><p>It had over 300 upvotes in just 20 minutes before being deleted.</p><p>『Why the Chungnam Branch Was Terrorized.fact』</p><p>「First off, I’m a former Hunter from the Chungnam Branch. Now I work in the private sector. I’m not gonna verify myself, so if you don’t believe me, just fuck off.</p><p>I’ll give you my take on the recent terror attack since you Hunter maniacs are probably curious.</p><p>Everyone who’s in the know already knows this, but the relationship between Hunter-turned-Association executives and non-Hunter executives has always been shit.</p><p>The Chungnam Branch Director is a textbook example of a high-ranking non-Hunter executive. She started as a clerk and climbed to Branch Director in just five years—must’ve had some insane political pull, right?</p><p>In fact, the Chungnam Branch was where the most corruption scandals were exposed, and a bunch of Hunter-turned-execs got caught up in them and were expelled en masse.</p><p>Naturally, rumors spread within the branch that the then-Department Head—now the current Branch Director—had fabricated the corruption cases to take down the Hunter execs who looked down on her and didn’t get along with her.</p><p>Then, a year later, the former Branch Director got tangled in a corruption scandal himself, resigned, and the Department Head took over.</p><p>So what’s the first thing she did? She purged all the high-ranking Hunter execs. Now, most of the Chungnam Branch’s department heads and above are non-Hunters. She did throw a few bones to the Hunter execs by giving them director positions, but they were all powerless roles in charge of random administrative busywork.</p><p>You think they just took that lying down? The hot new private Hunter company ‘Nemesis’? That’s the one the former Branch Director and all the ousted execs—plus the ones who quit—started up. You know this, right?</p><p>Of course, the Chungnam Branch’s gate exploration took a nosedive with all the A and B-rank Hunters bailing. They’re barely staying afloat by borrowing Hunters from other branches.</p><p>But how the hell did she pull that off? There’s a rumor she’s tight with the central government.</p><p>You all know the Korean government treats the Association like shit, right? There’s a theory that the government backed her to keep the Association in check, and honestly? I buy it lmao.</p><p>Realistically, how could a non-Hunter civilian fabricate a massive corruption scandal like that without help from the police or prosecutors?</p><p>Long story short, the former Chungnam Branch Hunters have every reason to kill the current branch chief, and there’s probably still a truckload of Hunters inside colluding with them, lololol.</p><p>They’re making it look like some third-party terror attack, but obviously that’s bullshit. If you read what I wrote, you’ll get a rough idea of who’s pulling the strings, right?</p><p>If any of you get assigned to Chungnam Branch, refuse it no matter what. A junior told me the atmosphere there is fucked—Hunters openly disobey orders from non-Hunter executives, lololololol.</p><p>Believe who you want, don’t believe who you don’t, and everyone just rest up.”</p><p>‘This is a total mess…’</p><p>There was no evidence in the post, but it made far more sense and felt more real than any of the articles from the news or the Hunter Association.</p><p>“Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon has arrived. There are clothes prepared for you to change into inside.”</p><p>“Yes, thank you.”</p><p>Regret over accepting the request began to creep in.</p><p>‘This crazy bastard Yoon Seong-hyeon, blinded by money…’</p><p>When he thought about it deeply, it was undeniably strange.</p><p>The Association owned plenty of bunkers and safehouses, so why rent out an entire hotel?</p><p>In other words, even the personnel managing the bunkers and safehouses couldn’t be trusted.</p><p>It felt like this incident was the opening shot signaling the collapse of the Association’s system—barely held together by the charisma of a single president ever since Gates and Awakened first appeared.</p><p>“Haa…”</p><p>Anger toward his handler began to well up.</p><p>Even if he was the one who accepted, he couldn’t help but wonder about the handler’s intentions for dumping this request on him without a single word of advice, as if it were nothing.</p><p>‘Did no one else want to do this, and I got stuck with the shitty job?’</p><p>Dwelling on negative thoughts would only frustrate him, so he decided to focus on the task at hand.</p><p>“Yes, Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon’s identity has been confirmed. If you go straight down that hallway, you’ll find the changing room.”</p><p>After passing the Association member’s inspection at the first-floor entrance, he entered the hotel and followed the hallway.</p><p>There were over ten Hunters in the first-floor lobby alone.</p><p>‘The Central Branch sent twenty, and it looks like other branches sent people too… The handler didn’t mention that…’</p><p>When he arrived at the changing room, there was a suit with his name on it.</p><p>He changed into the suit, received instructions on how to use the walkie-talkie from an Association member, and was told to go to the 14th floor, so he took the elevator up.</p><p>Ding—</p><p>When the elevator doors opened, two familiar faces stood before him.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, it’s been a while.”</p><p>Lee Seung-jun greeted him with a smile.</p><p>“Yes, Seung-jun, long time no see.”</p><p>And beside him was Min Se-rin.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon… hello…”</p><p>“Yes, Se-rin, it’s been a while.”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290738" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Min Se-rin’s expression was dark.</p><p>Beyond dark—her under-eyes were packed with dark circles, as if she’d been sick recently or hadn’t been eating well, and she looked haggard.</p><p>‘What the hell… did something happen?’</p><p>Lee Seung-jun explained the situation to me.</p><p>The Chungnam Branch Director and his family were on the 16th floor, with two bodyguards stationed on each floor. Min Se-rin and I were assigned to monitor the 14th floor for any suspicious activity.</p><p>All the hotel room doors on the 14th floor were wide open.</p><p>After finishing his explanation, Lee Seung-jun headed up to the 16th floor.</p><p>Min Se-rin and I just had to check every room and hallway every 30 minutes and report if anything was out of the ordinary.</p><p>‘If nothing happens for a week, this really is a cushy gig… but the supervisor’s briefing was way too half-assed.’</p><p>I couldn’t help but think he should’ve at least explained the current situation with the Chungnam Branch to me.</p><p>***</p><p>The first three days passed surprisingly quietly.</p><p>But then I heard some absolute bullshit from Lee Seung-jun.</p><p>Turns out, most of the Hunters dispatched from Central HQ—including Lee Seung-jun—were here on direct orders from the Association President. Only four of us, myself included, had actually accepted the supervisor’s proposal and taken the job.</p><p>He also mentioned that there was a risk of follow-up terrorist attacks, making this a dangerous mission for the pay we were getting.</p><p>Then he added, almost as an afterthought, that he was surprised I’d accepted.</p><p>He didn’t say much else, but the message was clear: ‘You got played, you idiot. The supervisor just used you to pad his stats. LOL.’</p><p>‘Fuck… Seong-hyeon, you absolute moron… Do you just get screwed over every damn day even as an A-rank?’</p><p>Self-loathing and rage toward the supervisor surged through me.</p><p>Fortunately, the first three days went smoothly, and Lee Seung-jun even said the remaining four would probably pass without incident. But that didn’t stop my blood from boiling.</p><p>‘Goddamn it… I’m going straight to that supervisor the second this is over.’</p><p>“Haa…”</p><p>During the two rest days, I was stuck in the hotel room assigned to me.</p><p>They delivered meals, even brought me a fresh suit every day.</p><p>Of course, calls to the outside were impossible.</p><p>‘Now that I think about it…’</p><p>Min Se-rin’s dark expression had been bothering me, but I never got around to asking her about it over those three days.</p><p>We’d worked together a few times before, but prying into her personal business felt… off. So I kept my mouth shut.</p><p>‘Is she sick or something?’</p><p>“Worry about yourself first, you idiot…”</p><p>Still in my robe, I plopped down into the massage chair provided in the room.</p><p>Wiiing—</p><p>The thought that all I could do for the next two days was sit in this chair, get massages, and eat the food they brought me was depressing as hell.</p><p>‘I’d rather be working.’</p><p>Ding-dong—</p><p>Just then, the doorbell to my hotel room rang.</p><p>‘Who the hell is it at this hour?’</p><p>I walked over to the door and asked who it was.</p><p>“Who is it…?”</p><p>“It’s… me, Min Se-rin…”</p><p>“Huh? Se-rin, what brings you—just a second, please.”</p><p>I hastily pulled on shorts and a tank top before opening the door.</p><p>“…”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290739" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Min Se-rin stood there, looking even more haggard than the first time I’d seen her, as if she had something to say.</p><p>In her hands was a plastic bag, stuffed full of something.</p><p>“Uh… Se-rin?”</p><p>Min Se-rin stared at the floor for a moment, then suddenly lifted the bag and said,</p><p>“Do you… want to drink?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>***</p><p>‘What the hell is going on…?’</p><p>I couldn’t bring myself to refuse, so we ended up drinking in my room.</p><p>The bag Min Se-rin brought contained alcohol and cans of nuts.</p><p>The problem was… the alcohol was *Drops*.</p><p>Hunters have such high tolerance that regular civilian alcohol barely does more than make their faces flush, so if they actually want to get drunk, they have to get their hands on *Drops*—moonshine brewed from Gate materials.</p><p>Naturally, producing and drinking *Drops* is illegal, but as long as no one causes trouble, the authorities don’t crack down, and the Hunter Association just turns a blind eye.</p><p>‘Well… how do you even stop people from drinking? But how did she get this here?’</p><p>This was only the second time I’d seen it since graduating from the training academy.</p><p>“Uh… but how did you get *Drops*?”</p><p>“Seung-jun sunbae gave it to me…”</p><p>“…”</p><p>I stared at Min Se-rin, completely lost.</p><p>“Ah… I haven’t been able to sleep lately, so Seung-jun sunbae told me to drink this and rest when I take breaks…”</p><p>“Oh…”</p><p>‘Then why the hell can’t you sleep…?’</p><p>I grabbed two glass cups, poured the drinks, and we started drinking in silence.</p><p>“Kgh—”</p><p>It hit completely different from soju or beer.</p><p>Min Se-rin emptied her glass, then refilled and drank it again on her own.</p><p>I figured I had to ask.</p><p>“Uh… Se-rin, is something wrong?”</p><p>Min Se-rin answered my question in her own way.</p><p>“Hng…”</p><p>“…?”</p><p>“Huuu—!”</p><p>Min Se-rin suddenly burst into tears in front of me.</p><p>‘What the actual fuck.’</p>
